page.layout: One running-text column, with a running head above it and a footnote below. Running head "JOH. MORINI." with page number 85 at top right. Under the column: the footnote "(s) In Epist. ad Leon. Allat." at left, the gathering signature "E 7." at centre right, and the catchword "esse" at far right.

main_text.p: tiquissimos ordinandorum Clericorum ritus Latinos, quorum nonnulli è Codicibus mille annorum & nongentorum ætatem superantibus, multi octingentorum; Græcos septem, qui tamen antiquissimis Latinis ætate sint inferiores, quorum primus ac vetustissimus è Codice Barberino exscriptus fuerat, secundum habuerat ex Monasterio Cryptæ Ferratensis, tertium & quartum è Bibliotheca Vaticana: & animadverit, non omnes in illis ordinationes repræsentari, sed præcipuas tantum; quintum è Codice Sancti Andreæ Vallensis exscriptum fuisse testatur; sextum è Bibliotheca Regia; septimum denique, qui recentior est & omnium amplissimus, ad eum miserat ipsemet Leo Allatius, quæ omnia à Morino Latino sermone donata sunt, & variis Annotationibus illustrata: Ex horum, inqvit, {s} comparatione manifestum est, eodem plane modo ordinationes sacras apud utramque gentem antiquitus factas esse, & quæ nonnulli Scholastici opinantur

page.notes: The first word "tiquissimos" is a fragment: the printed line begins with "tiqvissimos", the start of "antiquissimos" lies on the previous page. The catchword "esse" at the foot is the first word of the next page. The image also shows "inqvit" with q, normalised to "inquit" in the text. The text is printed with long s, which is transcribed as plain s. The mark "(s)" is the reference in the text and in the footnote. No marginal notes. Show-through and the scan edge at the right are not transcribed.
